dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Huh... This place has some similarities with the Abyss — a fully independent realm, separated from the outside world.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I suppose it wouldn't hurt to stay awhile. Make sure you leave plenty of open space for me to use. That way, I won't run the risk of damaging the landscape or buildings during my sword practice.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I can't quite get used to it. The level of Abyssal energy in Teyvat is quite low, but here, it's even lower still. It makes it hard for me to replenish the energy lost from training.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Of course, it's well within my abilities to connect this place directly to the Abyss, but... I'm sure you'd rather keep things peaceful and quiet here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm sorry... Is there anything we can do?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: No need to worry. Spending some time here isn't without its benefits. I'll just treat it as a rehearsal.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Rehearsal for what?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: We don't always get to pick where we fight our battles. Sometimes, we have to fight in conditions that don't suit us. In a similar vein, Master once told me that we can't rely on one form of power forever.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: "If losing one source of power reduces you to a helpless heap, then you never deserved that power to begin with."

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: This place may slowly drain the Abyssal power from my body, but in exchange, I can hone my swordsmanship in a purer form. In that sense, it benefits me.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: So, despite not being used to it, I'm quite happy to stay here a while longer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: If you find yourself having time for small talk, you should be spending it on refining your martial prowess instead.

choices.text: Hey, a quick chat never killed anyone!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: *sigh*...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: What would you like to ask?

choices.text: Don't you get lonely being by yourself?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Lonely, huh... Good question.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Humans are often plagued by loneliness. Some call it the "most agonizing emotion of all." I was once in the same boat, but now, I've basically sealed it away through rationality.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: After conquering my own loneliness, it got me thinking further. Why do we feel lonely at all? Why would such a negative emotion be retained over our eons of evolution?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I concluded that it must be because humans have always lived in communities. Loneliness serves no positive function on an individual level, but it has been beneficial for the survival of the species as a whole.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Master and I, however, have both evolved individually. Ours has been a different path, away from the collective of humanity.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: That's why I occasionally observe humans — to consider which useless emotions would be beneficial for me to keep. After all, it is helpful to retain a base ability to empathize with others.

choices.text: Have you ever experienced anything... fun?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: So, you're still trying to understand me. I... I wouldn't say that I've had many "fun" experiences in my life. The last time I had fun was way, way back.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: When I was little, there was a giant lizard that lived in the woods by my house. It wasn't afraid of humans — it was actually quite friendly with them.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: My mom said that it was hundreds of years old. Don't know if that's true or not. All I know is, it did look pretty old, and spent all its days sunbathing in the treetops.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I loved exploring the forest as a child. One day, I was chased by a swarm of hornets, each one the size of my palm. In desperation, I ran to the lizard and begged it for help.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: To my surprise, the lizard was helpless against the hornets too, so we just ran together, away from the swarm. I was faster, and managed to dive into a river, escaping the danger. When I returned to check up on the lizard, it had collapsed upon the ground.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I thought it had died, and cried bitter tears as I held it in my arms. I was so devastated that I gave it a proper burial, and even tried to set up a stele in lieu of a tombstone.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: But before I could finish, my mom caught me. She immediately dug the old lizard out, dressed its wounds, and brought it back from the brink of oblivion.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: After that, it continued to be friendly with all humans... all except me. Every time it saw me, it would flee like the wind.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I... don't even know if it survived that fire.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Hmm... Your power to "purify" the Abyss — I'm curious about how I'd tackle that if I ever faced it in battle. Needless to say, I'd have to adapt my strategy.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Well, there is only one way to find out...

choices.text: Wait, you mean to test it out...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Eh, maybe not now. If we both used our full strength, I doubt even this adepti contraption could withstand the force of our clash.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Let's save that fight for another time and place. For now, I'd like to discuss another matter with you.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: When faced with the Abyss, most creatures either fall victim to its corruption, or — like me — adapt and learn to wield it for themselves.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: You, of course, possess a very special power. Do you have any plans as to how you'd like to use it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I have used this power to help others.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: An unsurprising answer. It proves that you're still committed to justice and compassion.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Many people believe they would help others in a time of crisis, yet when they obtain the power to do so, concern themselves only with personal gain.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: What do you think best explains that? A weak will? Or the all-corrupting nature of power?

choices.text: I think you need a firm and steadfast heart.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Master once said that for humans, all roads lead back to the self.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: But I suppose that's not an absolute — not when there are those like you who are still willing to use their power to help others.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Alright, let's leave the discussion here for now. Deep conversations can guide us and help us see the way, but they shouldn't distract us from our training.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I'll start my drills now — let me know if you'd like to join.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Everyone experiences desires that they will not speak aloud.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: When they are too weak to realize these desires, they remain concealed deep within their hearts. But when they are strong, the floodgates will open, and all forms of vice come rushing out.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: We cannot expect everyone to stay true to their principles, which is why we constrain ourselves with laws.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Skirk.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Morning. If you have some free time today, come over and train with me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Skirk.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Mm, I can see the fatigue in your face. Go get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: There was a time when all I wanted was to learn everything there was to know. Explore every corner of the universe, witness all kinds of strange creatures and natural phenomena.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: And although that desire is long gone, the sight of this carefully curated collection does make me a little nostalgic.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Perhaps I should meditate here... Might be more soothing for both my mind and body.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Not too long ago, I dreamed of a place much like this.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Ever since I mastered the way of rationality, I have forbidden myself from dreaming. All it does is hinder my recovery from training. Yet on occasion, the dreams still come without warning. Sometimes, even rationality cannot fully suppress projections of the subconscious mind.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: If I'm honest... what I desire right now is to stay and rest for a while in this tranquil place.
